summary: LocoMuJoCo is a whole-body control benchmark centered on imitation learning, with optional pure RL. It supports MuJoCo CPU environments and MJX vectorized environments, plus an optional MjWarp backend for faster GPU simulation. The high-level entrypoints for downstream integration are the environment registry, task factories, trajectory loading pipeline, and training example folders.

Use imitation tasks when you need mocap trajectory playback or mimic training.

summary: The package is organized by responsibility. algorithms contains single-file JAX training algorithms. core contains the low-level MuJoCo and MJX environment runtime, observations, rewards, domain randomization, terrain, wrappers, and control functions. environments contains robot-specific env definitions. task_factories is the preferred high-level construction layer. trajectory handles dataset ingestion and alignment. smpl handles AMASS/retargeting. examples contains tutorials and train/eval scripts.

summary: The package root exposes Mujoco, Mjx, the task factories, and path helpers. PATH_TO_CUSTOM_MODELS is resolved from LOCOMUJOCO_MODELS_PATH in a YAML file and defaults to ~/.loco-mujoco-caches/models. get_registered_envs() returns the environment registry populated by environment modules at import time.

summary: Importing loco_mujoco.environments pulls in all humanoid and quadruped modules, each of which registers one or more environment classes into LocoEnv.registered_envs. Integration agents should treat env names as registry keys, not infer them dynamically from file names.

integration_notes: When adding a new robot, it must be imported and registered from the relevant __init__.py to become factory-visible.

summary: The documented built-in environments are 12 humanoid-style models and 4 quadrupeds. All listed envs have MJX-enabled variants. Humanoids with default mocap datasets include Atlas, Talos, UnitreeH1, UnitreeH1v2, UnitreeG1, Apollo, BoosterT1, ToddlerBot, FourierGR1T2, SkeletonTorque, SkeletonMuscle, and MyoSkeleton. Quadrupeds include UnitreeA1, UnitreeGo2, BDSpot, and AnymalC, but their mocap/pretrained datasets are marked pending in the overview.

integration_notes: If you need imitation data out of the box, start from the humanoid envs with mocap availability.
Quadrupeds are available as env classes even when dataset support is limited.

summary: ImitationFactory.make is the main high-level API for trajectory-driven environments. It builds the env from a registered env name, then loads and concatenates one or more trajectories from default datasets, AMASS, LAFAN1, or a custom Trajectory object. The default terminal handler is RootPoseTrajTerminalStateHandler and the default init handler is TrajInitialStateHandler.

How do I create imitation env
How do I mix multiple datasets

integration_notes: For external robot/action-set integration, custom_dataset_conf is the cleanest path if you already have a Trajectory object.
Default datasets are fetched from the HuggingFace dataset repo and optionally cached after conversion/interpolation.

summary: RLFactory.make creates a registered environment without expert trajectories. Its defaults are goal-conditioned locomotion: DefaultInitialStateHandler, HeightBasedTerminalStateHandler, GoalRandomRootVelocity, and TargetVelocityGoalReward. This is the correct entrypoint when the downstream agent wants locomotion control without a demonstration dataset.

integration_notes: Override goal_type, reward_type, init_state_type, or terminal_state_type when porting to custom training stacks.
If the target policy is imitation-based, do not start from RLFactory unless you explicitly want reward-only training.

summary: Dataset configuration is formalized as dataclasses. DefaultDatasetConf uses task, dataset_type in {mocap, pretrained}, and debug. AMASSDatasetConf accepts rel_dataset_path or dataset_group. LAFAN1DatasetConf accepts dataset_name or dataset_group. CustomDatasetConf wraps a Trajectory object. These are the objects to serialize or synthesize if another agent needs to instantiate an env programmatically.

summary: TrajectoryHandler is the core adapter between a dataset and the current MuJoCo model. It filters joints/bodies/sites that do not exist in the current model, extends missing ones with dummy entries, reorders data to match model ordering, and interpolates the trajectory to the control frequency. This is a key file for debugging mismatches between an imported motion dataset and a robot XML/model.

integration_notes: When integrating a community motion set, joint-name mismatch issues will usually surface here.
If you create custom trajectories, make sure names are consistent enough for filter_and_extend to align them.

summary: LocoEnv is the common robot environment base, built on top of Mjx/Mujoco runtime. It handles loaded trajectories, playback, dataset generation, reset/step carry with trajectory state, and convenience helpers such as play_trajectory. It also contains the deprecated generate/make path, but current code should prefer task factories. If an integration needs to understand how trajectory-following is fused into runtime state, this file is the main reference.

integration_notes: Trajectory-aware done/reset behavior is implemented here, not only in factories.

summary: Concrete robot env classes follow a repeatable pattern: load a default XML or provided MjSpec, derive default observation and action specs, optionally mutate the spec for MJX, then call the base environment constructor. UnitreeH1 is a representative example of how a new humanoid env is structured. It shows where to define default observations, actuator selection, XML path resolution, and any robot-specific spec pruning such as disabling arms or back joints.

integration_notes: Use an existing robot close to your hardware morphology as the starting template.
For new robots, the minimum useful implementation usually includes XML path, observation spec, action spec, root body metadata, and optional MJX simplifications.

summary: Shared robot bases encode morphology-level defaults. BaseRobotHumanoid defines default mimic sites such as pelvis, limbs, and hands, and uses pelvis as the root body. BaseRobotQuadruped uses trunk as root and leaves mimic sites empty. These bases are relevant when adapting reward, goal, or imitation site selection across robot families.

summary: Low-level behavior is split inside core. Change observation composition under core/observations. Change reward logic under core/reward. Change goal vectors under the goal-related observation/reward modules and RL factory defaults. Change init and terminal logic under initial_state_handler and terminal_state_handler. Domain randomization and terrain logic live under their dedicated subpackages. This directory is the primary place for non-robot-specific behavior changes.

summary: Training examples are grouped by algorithm family. jax_rl is a pure RL PPO example on UnitreeGo2 using GoalRandomRootVelocity and locomotion-style rewards. jax_gail is a minimal GAIL example on UnitreeH1 using GoalTrajMimic. jax_amp is an AMP example on UnitreeH1 using GoalTrajRootVelocity and TargetVelocityTrajReward. jax_rl_mimic is a DeepMimic-style PPO imitation example on UnitreeH1 using GoalTrajMimic and MimicReward. Each example folder contains conf.yaml, experiment.py, eval.py, and a README.

integration_notes: For quickest downstream hookup, clone the closest example directory instead of writing a training loop from scratch.

summary: The tutorials folder is the fastest way to answer task-specific usage questions. 00 replays datasets. 01 creates a MuJoCo env. 02 creates an MJX env and is the reference for vectorized execution. 04 shows Gymnasium wrapping. 05 and 06 customize observation space and grouping. 07 changes control type. 08 covers domain randomization. 09 covers terrain. 10 creates a custom trajectory. 11 creates custom modules. There is no 03 file in the examples folder.

summary: The smpl package is responsible for AMASS installation and retargeting workflows. ImitationFactory delegates AMASS loading through the retargeting layer, which also uses robot-specific configuration under smpl/robot_confs. If the integration task is about importing a human motion dataset into a robot env, this is the relevant subsystem after the basic task factory flow.

integration_notes: Community motion datasets that are not already in LocoMuJoCo format may need conversion through this layer or through a custom Trajectory pipeline.
If the source data is already robot-joint-space data, prefer CustomDatasetConf before touching SMPL.

summary: Default LocoMuJoCo datasets and LAFAN1 are pulled from the HuggingFace dataset repository robfiras/loco-mujoco-datasets. AMASS is not auto-downloaded due to licensing. The project also supports precomputing caches for forward-kinematics-derived dataset fields using the loco-mujoco-set-all-caches command. Default cache and custom model paths are persisted through YAML variables under the package directory.

summary: For other agents, the recommended retrieval sequence is: find the closest env or example; then inspect the matching factory; then inspect the robot env class; then inspect trajectory or core modules only if the task involves dataset mismatch or custom reward/goal/runtime behavior. Use env names like UnitreeH1, UnitreeG1, UnitreeGo2, MjxUnitreeH1, and feature keywords like observation_spec, actuation_spec, domain_randomization, custom trajectory, MimicReward, GoalTrajMimic, and TargetVelocityGoalReward.
